topic: Socio-Religious Reform Movements of Indian History
description: During the 19th century, several reformist and revivalist movements emerged in Indian society based on rationalism and humanism. These movements aimed to eradicate social evils like the Sati system, child marriage, and untouchability, while promoting modern education and equality.

sections.title: Nature of Movements and Key Concepts
sections.description: Socio-religious movements of the 19th and 20th centuries were broadly divided into two main categories based on their approach to religious texts and modern ideas.

key_concepts.explanation: These movements were highly influenced by modern Western ideas and rationalism. They sought to modify religious practices to suit contemporary times. Examples include the Brahmo Samaj and the Aligarh Movement.

These movements believed in the fundamental purity of ancient religious texts and advocated a return to the original, uncorrupted form of their religion. Examples include the Arya Samaj and the Deoband Movement.

important_facts.fact: Raja Ram Mohan Roy is widely regarded as the 'Father of Indian Renaissance' and the 'Maker of Modern India'.

sections.title: Major Hindu Reform Movements
sections.description: The most influential socio-religious movements that began in Bengal and North India to reform Hinduism and society.

historical_events.significance: Established by Raja Ram Mohan Roy in Calcutta to propagate Monotheism (belief in one God) and fight against orthodox practices.
Founded by Raja Ram Mohan Roy to oppose idol worship and meaningless rituals. It was later led and expanded by Maharishi Debendranath Tagore and Keshub Chandra Sen.
Established by Swami Dayanand Saraswati in Bombay. Its guiding principle and most famous slogan was 'Go back to the Vedas'.
Founded by Swami Vivekananda in Belur (Bengal). It heavily emphasized social service, humanitarian relief, and the philosophy of Vedanta.

key_associations.extra_info: This book is the core ideological text of the Arya Samaj, detailing Vedic principles and critiquing orthodox religious dogmas.
These were highly influential magazines published by Swami Vivekananda in English and Bengali, respectively, to spread his teachings.

sections.title: Movements in Western and Southern India
sections.description: Prominent movements in Maharashtra and South India that heavily focused on dismantling the caste system and promoting social equality.

historical_events.significance: Established by Dr. Atmaram Pandurang in Bombay. It became highly popular and effective after the eminent scholar M.G. Ranade joined it.

historical_events.event: Foundation of Satyashodhak Samaj (Truth Seekers' Society)
historical_events.significance: Founded by Jyotirao Phule in Maharashtra to challenge Brahmanical supremacy and work for the socio-economic upliftment of lower castes and women.

key_associations.extra_info: Written in 1873, this groundbreaking book was dedicated to the American anti-slavery movement and drew parallels with the oppressive Indian caste system.
Started for the upliftment of the untouchable Ezhava community in Kerala. His famous slogan was: 'One religion, one caste, one God for mankind'.

key_associations.associated_with: Madam H.P. Blavatsky and Col. H.S. Olcott
key_associations.extra_info: Originally founded in New York, its headquarters shifted to Adyar (Madras) in 1882. Annie Besant later popularized the movement in India.

sections.title: Muslim and Parsi Reform Movements
sections.description: Movements aimed at introducing modern education, liberal ideas, and social reforms within the Muslim and Zoroastrian (Parsi) communities.

historical_events.significance: Initiated by Sir Syed Ahmad Khan to promote modern western education among Muslims. He founded the Mohammedan Anglo-Oriental College (later Aligarh Muslim University).
Founded by Dadabhai Naoroji, Naoroji Furdonji, and others to restore the purity of Zoroastrianism and significantly improve the social condition of Parsi women.

key_associations.extra_info: An Urdu journal started by him to propagate rational thoughts, scientific temper, and social reforms in Islamic society.
A Gujarati newspaper whose name means 'Truth Teller'. It served as the primary mouthpiece for the Parsi reform movement.
A reformist movement within Islam that sought to establish liberal principles, universal brotherhood, and strongly opposed the concept of violent Jihad.

sections.title: Important Social Reform Legislations
sections.description: Crucial laws passed by the British Indian Government, largely due to the relentless pressure and campaigns by Indian social reformers.

historical_events.significance: Governor-General Lord William Bentinck passed Regulation XVII, declaring the practice of Sati illegal and punishable, driven by Raja Ram Mohan Roy's campaign.
Passed during the tenure of Lord Canning, this historic act was primarily the result of the tireless efforts of Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar.
Passed due to the efforts of Parsi reformer B.M. Malabari, this act raised the minimum age of marriage for girls from 10 to 12 years.
Named after its sponsor Dr. Harbilas Sarda, this landmark act fixed the minimum age of marriage at 18 years for boys and 14 years for girls across all communities.
